children.value: > Fact From Story: Sam Bankman-Fried, the founder of failed cryptocurrency exchange FTX, is on trial for seven counts of wire fraud and conspiracy.
> > Fact From Story: FTX was a fraud “from the start,” the Securities and Exchange Commission alleges — with a “multi-billion-dollar deficiency caused by his own misappropriation of customer funds.”
> > > Fact From Story: The government has indicated FTX co-founder Gary Wang and engineering head Nishad Singh will also be among the witnesses called to give testimony about Bankman-Fried.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Testimony from co-conspirators can be used as evidence in a trial.
> > Commonsense Knowledge: Wire fraud and conspiracy are serious crimes that can result in significant penalties, including imprisonment.
> Fact From Story: Misplacing several billion is kicking over a lantern in Chicago in 1871.
> > Fact From Story: Bankman-Fried directed alleged co-conspirator Caroline Ellison to repay third-party loans and went on making investments.
> > Fact From Story: FTX was a fraud “from the start,” the Securities and Exchange Commission alleges — with a “multi-billion-dollar deficiency caused by his own misappropriation of customer funds.”
> > > > Fact From Story: Alameda had withdrawn assets that included the customer funds, Sun testified.
> > > > Commonsense Knowledge: Misappropriating customer funds is illegal.
> > Commonsense Knowledge: Directing misappropriated funds towards investments and loans is a form of conspiracy.
> Commonsense Knowledge: As the founder of FTX, Sam Bankman-Fried was responsible for overseeing the company's finances and ensuring its stability.
